question.prompt: Joey and Chloe and their daughter Zoe all have the same birthday. Joey is \(1\) year older than Chloe, and Zoe is exactly \(1\) year old today. Today is the first of the \(9\) birthdays on which Chloe’s age will be an integral multiple of Zoe’s age. What will be the sum of the two digits of Joey’s age the next time his age is a multiple of Zoe’s age?

solutions.title: Turn age multiples into divisor counts
solutions.explanation:
The age difference stays fixed, so the birthdays when one age divides another can be counted using divisors.

Let Chloe's age today be \(n\). In \(y\) years, where \(y\) is a nonnegative integer, her age divided by Zoe's age will be
\[
\frac{n+y}{1+y}=1+\frac{n-1}{1+y}.
\]
This is an integer exactly when \(1+y\) divides \(n-1\). As \(y\) runs through the nonnegative integers, \(1+y\) runs through all positive integers. Thus the nine specified birthdays mean that \(n-1\) has exactly nine positive divisors.

If an integer has prime factorization \(p_1^{e_1}\cdots p_r^{e_r}\), each divisor independently chooses an exponent from 0 through \(e_i\). Its divisor count is therefore \((e_1+1)\cdots(e_r+1)\). Since \(9=9=3\cdot3\), we must have
\[
n-1=p^8\quad\text{or}\quad n-1=p^2q^2,
\]
where \(p,q\) are distinct primes in the second case.

The question specifies that Joey's age at the next qualifying birthday has two digits. His current age is \(n+1\), so \(n-1<100\). The first form is impossible because \(p^8\ge2^8=256\). For the second form, the smallest product of distinct primes is \(2\cdot3=6\); every other such product is at least \(2\cdot5=10\). Hence the only possibility below 100 is
\[
n-1=2^2\cdot3^2=36.
\]
Chloe is 37 today, and Joey is 38.

For Joey, the corresponding age ratio in \(y\) years is
\[
\frac{38+y}{1+y}=1+\frac{37}{1+y}.
\]
Since 37 is prime, its positive divisors are 1 and 37. These give \(y=0\) and \(y=36\), so the next qualifying birthday is 36 years from today. Joey will be \(38+36=74\), whose digit sum is \(7+4=\boxed{11}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
